scope: P2-G3 people rows (R12, R36, R78, R910): speaker of every source quote, identity of every held author slug, 40 sampled 'none' decisions, every empty_reasons sentence. Brief items 2 and 4 out of scope.

findings.problem: The held row is not Macarius's own words. It is the 25 September reading of the Great Menaion, the Life and Praise of St Sergius, which other authors wrote and Macarius only compiled. Mark's rule needs words the Library holds from him. The same bands left out Macarius of Corinth and Macarius of Optina for exactly this reason (compiler or unsigned preface, no own words), so the drafts treat the cases inconsistently.
findings.evidence: cic/corpus-map/russian-church-stoglav-to-nikon.yaml, row with author macarius-metropolitan: work 'Great Menaion of Metropolitan Macarius, September 25: the Life and Praise of Saint Sergius', note 'Not read for this entry.' Compare R78 and R910 decisions on Macarius of Corinth ('co-compiled the Philokalia ... no text in his own words is held') and on Macarius of Optina.
findings.fix: Drop the held item. Back him with a source quote only if words of his own are found (for example in the Stoglav files, cic/texts/stoglav_stoglav-fra_duchesne1920.txt or stoglav_stoglav-chu_kozhanchikov1863.txt, which the shelf holds under slug stoglav). Otherwise record backing none.

findings.problem: The quote is labelled as the Gesta of the Council of Aquileia, but lines 3004-3005 are Kauffmann's own German introduction quoting the line second-hand ('Bündig antwortet er auf die frage des Ambrosius : qui sunt consortes uestri? P 298'). The edited minutes give the same words at line 14728. The draft's flag notes the quote occurs twice and that the first was used.
findings.evidence: cic/texts/auxentius-durostorum_epistula-de-fide-vita-obitu-wulfilae_kauffmann1899.txt:3004-3005 (editor's German introduction); :14728 '6 Ambrosius dixit: qui sunt consortes uestri? 25'
findings.fix: Point the source to lines 14728, quote 'qui sunt consortes uestri?'. The words stay Ambrose's own, recorded in the minutes.

findings.problem: He was left out on the ground that his chronicle 'survives within Michael the Syrian's later books, which the Library does not hold.' The Library holds Michael's tome 2 (books VIII-XI). There Michael quotes Dionysius in the first person and names him as the speaker. The editor's note also marks a whole chapter as taken from Dionysius. So the omission is wrong, and the movement's empty_reasons sentence ('does not yet hold words of their own from any of the people named here') is false for him.
findings.evidence: cic/texts/michael-the-syrian_chronique-tome2-livres-viii-xi-fra_chabot1901.txt:36788-36790 'Le patriarche Denys de Tell Mahré, qui rapporte ces choses, ajoute : « J'ai pris ces choses des histoires de Daniel, fils de Samuel, du Tour 'Abdîn, mon grand-père maternel.' (verified verbatim, whitespace squashed); :27772 'est tiré de Denys de Tell Mahrê. C'est le seul chapitre de sa Chronique dont nous ayons le texte.'
findings.fix: Add a source item: name 'Dionysius of Tel Mahre', voice 1, quote "J'ai pris ces choses des histoires de Daniel, fils de Samuel, du Tour 'Abdîn, mon grand-père maternel." at 36788-36790. Kind: own-writing, a fragment preserved by Michael. Set the year from his patriarchate, which began in 818; check that date against the entry or the file before use. Remove the movement from empty_reasons.

findings.problem: 'Its story is carried by communities, councils and documents rather than named individuals.' reads as a claim about the history, not about this entry. For the struggle against apartheid, the Anglican Communion or the suppressed Romanian Greek Catholic church, a reader knows named people led them, so the card misleads. The true reason is narrower: this entry's voices list names only bodies and documents.
findings.evidence: Census voices for these six movements name only bodies or documents (e.g. 'The Kairos Theologians', 'Decree 358 of 1 December 1948', 'The Lambeth Conference of 1920'); no individual decision exists for any of them.
findings.fix: Say what is true of the entry, for example: 'This entry draws on councils, churches and documents, not on any one person's words, so no one is shown.'

findings.target: joachimite-current / Gerard of Borgo San Donnino
findings.problem: The work is labelled 'Introductorius', but Denifle's footnote 2 gives the passage as 'a gloss cited by the commission of Anagni'. The words reach us only through the hostile commission's protocol, so they are attributed, not his own writing directly.

findings.fix: Relabel the work as 'a gloss cited by the commission of Anagni, in Denifle, Archiv I', and add a flag: attributed, preserved by the commission.

findings.problem: The words are Julian's, but the label names only Warfield's essay. Warfield's footnote gives the primary text: Augustine's Unfinished Work iii.82. The R12 flag already says this.
findings.fix: Label it 'Julian, as quoted in Augustine's Unfinished Work iii.82, in B. B. Warfield's introduction (NPNF 1/5)'. If the Library holds a primary text, use that instead.

findings.problem: The held row is his Gothic Bible, a translation of Scripture. It is his work, but not his own words. R12 backs him in homoian-arian-christianity with his own creed.
findings.evidence: cic/corpus-map/gothic-and-vandal-homoian-christianity.yaml row by wulfila ('The Gothic Bible of Wulfila'); cic/texts/auxentius-durostorum_epistula-de-fide-vita-obitu-wulfilae_kauffmann1899.txt:7431 'ego ulfila episkopus et confessor semper sie credidi'
findings.fix: Either keep the held row and add a flag ('translation'), or back him the same way R12 does, with the creed quote. Make the two bands consistent.

findings.target: syriac-edessa-nisibis and bardaisanite-current / Bardaisan; alexandria-catechetical / Pantaenus; church-of-the-east-under-the-mongols / Rabban Bar Sauma; the-hesychast-revival / Mitrofan
findings.problem: In these held rows other people set down the words. Bardaisan's dialogue was written by his disciple Philip (the shelf note says so). Pantaenus's 'Fragments' are later writers' reports. Bar Sauma's row is an anonymous Life that abridges his lost Persian account. Mitrofan's row is a Life compiled at Neamt from his account. Each is the same named person, not a namesake, and the R12, R36 and R78 reasons or flags disclose the Pantaenus, Sauma and Mitrofan cases. Bardaisan's two rows carry no such flag.
findings.evidence: Shelf notes: syriac-edessa-nisibis bardesan row ('penned by his disciple Philippus'); church-of-the-east-under-the-mongols yahballaha-sauma row; the-hesychast-revival-paisius-and-the-philokalia mitrofan-schemamonk row.
findings.fix: Add a 'reported' flag to both Bardaisan items, as was done for Pantaenus. No change of backing is needed.

checked: Scripted: all 141 source quotes re-verified verbatim at their stated lines (whitespace squashed): 0 misses. All 287 held items: the row_id exists on cic/corpus-map/<movement>.yaml and its author slug equals the item's: 0 mismatches. Every name is a substring of its voices line: 0 failures. Judged by hand: opened the context (about 8-14 lines before each quote) for every doubtful source quote, about 45 of them, to confirm who is speaking. The rest I confirmed from the work heading or the attribution inside the quote ('Ego frater Petrus...', 'I William Sautre...', 'X dixit:'). For held rows, I read the work title of all 287 and the shelf note of 14 doubtful rows (biographies, compilations, attributed works, joint works). None decisions: a seeded random sample of 40 (28 individuals, 12 non-individuals), each read against its voices line and its shelf's author list. For likely misses I checked cic/texts filenames and grepped the one Library file that could hold the person (Michael the Syrian, Book of the Himyarites). Found 1 wrong omission (F3). Kaleb's omission is correct: Moberg says the prayer of Kaleb is in the Greek Acta, not in the Book of the Himyarites. Empty_reasons: all 164 sentences read (104 share one sentence, 27 another).
